sentences.text:
This Miscellaneous Appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, being aggrieved of award dated 30.07.2013, passed by learned 13th Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal (M.P.), whereby, learned Tribunal has awarded meager amount of Rs.77,000/-, on account of an accident which took place on 26.11.2011, when claimant Mangal Singh Meena was travelling on his motorcycle towards Bairagarhkala, when in front of Akash hut, Maruti WagonR bearing registration No.MP-09-CJ-8777, being driven rashly and negligently had caused accident.
This accident resulted in fracture of his left leg.
He had sustained crush injuries of the ankle and other injuries on hand and other parts of the body.

FIR registering case Crime No.257/11 was Mangal Singh Meena vs Umesh Khonkar on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116431351/
1 registered vide Ex.P/1.

entities.text: Mangal Singh Meena vs Umesh Khonkar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After investigation, charge sheet was filed, vehicle was seized and accused was arrested.

2. Claimant had taken treatment at various hospitals and had examined Dr. Manish Gupta (PW/2),
who found that there was a crushed injury on the left leg joint and movement of the ankle was only 10%.
Power of the muscles was less than normal.
44.6% permanent disability was certified by the doctor.

3. It is submitted that learned Claims Tribunal has not even considered the aspect of amount spent by the claimant on his treatment and arbitrarily those bills have been rejected on a hypothetical finding that treatment could not have been taken simultaneously at two hospitals, namely, Apex Hospital and LBS Hospital as mentioned in para 20 of the award.
4. It is submitted that in fact, claimant was admitted in Apex Hospital.
He was taking treatment at Apex Hospital, but in the meanwhile for certain tests and examination, he was referred to LBS Hospital, where he remained admitted from 02.01.2012 to 05.01.2012.
There are no overlapping bills of treatment between for this duration when he was at LBS Hospital.
It is submitted that he was in Apex Hospital from 26.11.2011 to 21.01.2012 and for the intervening period of four days, he was at LBS Hospital.
Various prescriptions, cash memos etc. have been exhibited from Ex.P/96 to P/422.

These bills have not been disputed and are duly supported with prescription of the Apex Hospital starting from Ex.P/1-82 to Ex.P/3-89.
5.
Thus, taking these facts into consideration, request is made to enhance compensation under different heads including payment of compensation for the expenditure incurred on treatment.

6. Shri T.S. Lamba, learned counsel for respondent No.3-ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co.
Ltd., in his turn, submits that Tribunal has rightly mentioned in para 23 that prescriptions starting from P-1/82 to Ex.P/3-89 are not duly signed by the treating doctor.

sentences.text: Therefore, no indulgence be shown and award be maintained as it is.
7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, as far as Ex.P/11 is concerned, it is issued by the Apex Hospital.
It is dated 21.01.2012.
It has shown the date of admission as 26.11.2011 and date of discharge as 21.01.2012.
It bears seal and signature of the hospital.
Comprehensively, it reflects that a sum of Rs.1,60,000/- was paid towards treatment.
Similarly, Ex.P/12 is towards the various investigation which were carried out and which is for a sum of Rs.4,000/-.
Discharge card of the LBS Hospital is on record as Ex.P/9.
Discharge summary of Apex Hospital is on record as Ex.P/8.

When all these facts are taken into consideration, then total of the bills which are authenticated comes out to Rs.2,97,550/- (Rupees Two Lacs Ninety Seven Thousand, Five Hundred and Fifty).
8.

These amounts are payable as it is not the allegation of any of the respondents that these bills or vouchers are forged or are not pertaining to treatment which is also borne out from various X-rays which have been brought on record as Ex.P/412, Ex./P/413, Ex.P/414, Ex.P/415, Ex.P/416,
Ex.P/417, SAN Ex.P/418 and C.T. Scan report.

Therefore, this Court has no hesitation to allow these Mangal Singh Meena vs Umesh Khonkar on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116431351/
2 bills to the extent of Rs.2,97,550/-(Rupees Two Lacs, Ninety Seven Thousand, Five Hundred and Fifty).

entities.text: Mangal Singh Meena vs Umesh Khonkar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In fact, Ex.P/11 supports the contention of the appellant that he was referred by the Apex Hospital to LBS Hospital, because the amount which was paid by the Apex Hospital to LBS Hospital and which has been charged from the claimant is mentioned in Ex.P/11.

Therefore, the aspect of taking treatment simultaneously at two hospitals gets answered in terms of Ex.P/11.
9.
As far as amounts under various heads are concerned, Tribunal has only paid a sum of Rs.75,000/- under the head of special diet, mental and physical agony, attender and transportation.
No amount has been awarded under the head of fracture.
A sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under the head of fracture.
10. No amount is awarded under the head of loss of income during the period of treatment.
11. The claimant was admittedly working as a driver.
On the date of the accident, wages even for a semi-skilled labourer were to the tune of Rs.4,675/- per month.

Looking to the nature of the injury,
for loss of earning capacity, a sum of Rs.28,050/- will be payable under the head for a period of six months @ Rs.4675/- per month.
12. Though it is argued by Shri Lamba that there is no evidence to show that claimant was a skilled driver, but the fact is that there is no denial to this effect also.
Merely non-production of driving licence is not a circumstance to hold otherwise.
In cross-examination, this witness has denied the suggestion that he was not in a private job as a driver and was not earning Rs.15,000/-.
13. It is true that there is no proof of the income @ Rs.15,000/- per month.

But, even if calculation is made as per the rates admissible for a semi-skilled labourer, then when disability certificate Ex.P/7 issued by the District Medical Board, Bhopal, is taken into consideration, then doctors have certified about 52% disability of left leg.

Taking this fact into consideration that doctor Gupta has opined about restriction of movement in the ankle, pain and swelling etc., 10% functional disability can be considered for the purposes of computation of notional compensation on account of loss of earning capacity.
14. Since this Court has taken notional income at Rs.4675/- per month, then 10% of it will come out to Rs.467.50 per month or Rs.5610/- per annum.

Age of the claimant as per the Claim Petition is 34 years, whereas, in the discharge card issued by the LBS Hospital Ex.P/9, it is mentioned as 40 years and so also in Ex.P/8, which is discharge summary of Apex Hospital, therefore, the disability certificate which is issued on 12.08.2012, his age is mentioned as 42 years.
Therefore, on the date of the accident, his age was more than 40 years, but less than 41 years.
15. Therefore, taking this fact into consideration that he was more than 40 years, 25% is to be added towards the future prospects.
Then multiplier of 14 will be applicable, taking total compensation under the head of loss of earning capacity at Rs.98,175/- (Rupees Ninety Eight Thousand, One Hundred and Seventy Five).

Thus, claimant will be entitled to an additional sum of Rs.4,48,775/-
(Rupees Four Lacs, Forty Eight Thousand, Seven Hundred and Seventy Five), over and above, the amount awarded by learned Claims Tribunal.

This additional amount will carry interest @ 6% per Mangal Singh Meena vs Umesh Khonkar on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116431351/
3 annum.
16.
